newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela lauds S.Africa progress, vows more on way.
newsitem.headline: Mandela lauds S.Africa progress, vows more on way.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela opened parliament on Friday promising further progress on privatisation and lifting exchange controls in a speech that was broadly welcomed by financial markets.

"We are confident that we have moved into high gear in the implementation of the macro-economic strategy," Mandela said, referring to a government plan to achieve six percent growth and 500,000 new jobs a year by 2000.
South African stocks rose in response to Mandela's remarks and the local currency, which last month began to strengthen after an eight-month decline, made further gains.

Mandela promised tough action against crime, which has become possibly the most pressing social issue, vowed to streamline an inefficient and bloated civil service, and praised a new spirit of cooperation which he said was abroad in the country.

"We can all derive pride from the fact that we took a historic step last year throught the adoption of the new constitution, the basic law of our land reflecting the nation's yearning for a rising quality of life, in circumstances of democracy, peace and respect for human rights," Mandela said.

The final post-apartheid constitution took effect at midnight on Monday, the culmination of multi-party negotiations that began after the then president F.W. de Klerk declared six years ago this month that he would free Mandela from jail and legalise banned black liberation groups.
Mandela's African National Congress swept de Klerk from office in the country's first all-race election in April 1994.
Mandela said that since then his government had taken giant strides in providing water, electricity, housing and health facilities to the impoverished black masses.

"During the course of this year we shall further speed up the process of practical implementation. South Africa must become a beehive of communities acting to change their lives for the better," he said.
